items.title: Andy Anderson Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: he had a sister live over there, you know, her name was Bertha Jackson.

ctx.x: Yes, he's from my home. Yeah, he's a, daddy had a place out there on the highway, you know. And he was like, yeah he was a blues player, you know. I wasn't thinking about playing trumpet, but I had it in my mind, it was a dream then, you know. And I had it in my mind, but after the tournament, I'm surprised he ever thought that Tommy had got great. He was one of the greatest blues trumpet players ever in Chicago. I heard that. And Bunk used to come over to my home, see, on those weekends, sometimes he'd stay all…

In other words they'd play until they sold everything, the gum, the ham, the chicken, everything out. That's what the band played. The price of admission wasn't much then, a thirty cents or a forty cents or something like that. Yeah, Bunk was a great guy. I think he was a great, I'll tell you what Bunk's playing, I like about Bunk's playing in 5th. I mean it looked like he put all his whole heart, soul and mind on every note he made. Looked like he talked to them and so on. And it was great. He was great. And…
What about that fight between Big Cornish and Dad? You tell me about that once. Oh I'll tell you about Cornish and Dad.
